title: The Generalized Vanishing Conjecture: The Two-Variable Theorem and the First Failing Dimension
summary: Proves binary GVC with finite support certificates and a sharp operator-independent mixed cutoff, and constructs homogeneous failures in every dimension at least three.
verification: The added results have written proofs and local exact checks. The full binary theorem remains only partly formalized in Lean.
next_steps: Independent mathematical review of the binary proof and the support-certificate and cutoff results.
Fresh Lean replay and transitive axiom audit before claiming a newly replayed formal artifact.
abstract:
We determine the dimensions in which the Generalized Vanishing Conjecture
holds for constant-coefficient differential operators over a field of
characteristic zero.  In two variables, if
$\Lambda^m(P^m)=0$ for every positive integer $m$, then
$\Lambda^m(QP^m)=0$ for every fixed polynomial $Q$ and all sufficiently
large $m$, with no homogeneity assumption on $\Lambda$ or $P$.
The proof combines Hall's marriage theorem, Newton-face separation and
prime-adic isolation of a single endpoint contribution, using the
constant-term theorem of Duistermaat and van der Kallen.
It also gives a finite support certificate for the premise and the sharp
operator-independent cutoff
$m>(1+\lfloor(\deg P+1)^2/4\rfloor)\deg Q$.
In three variables we construct a homogeneous polynomial of degree twelve
for which all pure contractions under
$(4\partial_x\partial_y+\partial_t^2)^{6m}$ vanish, while multiplication
by $x^2$ gives a nonzero contraction at every positive power.
The construction extends Long's adjacent-coefficient mechanism to an
explicit homogeneous family.  Thus the unrestricted conjecture, and
already its homogeneous form, holds in dimension $n$ exactly when $n\leq2$.
